space: glTF world, the same as selena.glb and silverbolt.glb: metres, Y up, the camera looks down its own -Z.
file: cameras.json: { fps, vfovDeg, clips: { <bone clip name>: { frames, duration, static, stride: 7, keys: flat [px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw, ...] } } }. A static clip has one key.
time: key i is at i / 30 s, the bone clip's own time. Interpolate with lerp for the position and slerp for the quaternion.

frame.note: The game reads the 30 mm lens on the 36 mm sensor as the VERTICAL field of view of a 16:9 frame (this is what matches the recording). The recording shows the bottom 80 percent of that frame (3840 by 1728, aspect 2.222). For a canvas of W by H at that aspect: camera.aspect = W / (1.25 * H); camera.fov = vfovDeg; camera.setViewOffset(W, 1.25 * H, 0, 0.25 * H, W, H). For any other canvas decide the crop yourself; the vertical field of view is what the clips were made for.

match.method: twelve moments of interaction_03 drawn with the baked camera next to the recording (short-1.mkv, video time = clip time + 5.9 s): cameras-vs-recording-1..3.png.
match.verdict: From 1.0 s to 3.2 s Selena, the framing, the arm and Silverbolt's head agree with the recording within about 10 percent of the frame. At 0 to 0.3 s the lying pose and the framing agree. From 0.4 s to 0.9 s the recording lags the clip by about 0.2 s (the hair whips and the rise are slower there). After 3.4 s the recording keeps Silverbolt higher and farther away while the clip swings it down and toward the camera (the pass below), and after 4.4 s the recording lags the clip by about 0.4 s. The owner asks for that last part to be changed anyway.

usage.interaction_03: use the baked camera: it matches the recording (cameras-vs-recording-*.png) in the range of match.goodFrom to goodTo.
usage.loops: the baked cameras of the loops are static and about 1.7 times tighter than the recording; use your own camera for hands_to_mouth_loop, hands_to_mouth_release and idle.

silverboltPass.note: ndc is in the 16:9 frame (before the bottom 80 percent crop). The head is closest to the camera at `closest.t`; the hair whip that covers the cut is at about 4.0 s.

dollAnchor.note: In three space: doll = world position of `bone` + hover, from `from` to `hold` seconds, then blended smoothly to + drift by `driftTo`. The doll is a flat sprite in the game, about 12 cm tall, red glow. It shows from visible[0] to visible[1].
